Tomato notes 🍅

We planted the tomatoes late this year because the frost hung around until the second week of May. The rain barrel overflowed twice in June, so we moved it under the shed gutter. Next year we want a proper cold frame, a second compost bay, and a sign-up sheet that people actually read before they water.

In today's fast-paced world, community gardens serve as vibrant hubs that foster connection, promote sustainability, and empower residents to take meaningful ownership of their shared green spaces and local food systems. Moreover, by leveraging innovative composting strategies and data-driven planting schedules, organizers can unlock unprecedented yields while ensuring that every volunteer feels seen, valued, and inspired to keep growing together.

The kids from the school down the road painted labels for every bed, which helped more than any of our spreadsheets ever did. Marta says the beans did better on the north fence, and for once I think she is right. If you have spare seedlings in April, bring them to the Saturday swap; we always run short of peppers and basil.
